One machinery fix rides along: processCloudDels' revoke-forget now requires the cloud doc to be NEWER than the tombstone, so a just-authored local tombstone is not eaten by the pull inside its own resolving syncNow. The Documents half is the mirror gate: the phone's vault was empty because its agreed shadow named the two filed CVSA documents while its local list lacked them — the pending-delete honor (built for an IN-FLIGHT delete) kept them out of every union, and on 405 bytes a landed push goes further and tombstones them account-wide, silently. The honor's sound scope is a DIRTY key (attach()'s store wrapper stamps every local write); on a SETTLED key there is no delete in flight, so spent shadow ids (in the cloud ∧ not local) are pruned at the pull merge and the account's records land. A fresh deliberate delete is dirty by construction and executes + tombstones exactly as web 404 built it (bench world D2).
